answer: One defense is a refundable stake bonded to each identity: an agent must lock tokens before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if behavioral fingerprints show one operator behind several accounts. Like quartz veins running through rock, a single operator's habits leave a trace across identities that clustering can spot even when names differ. New identities start on a narrow ledge of trust, with tiny limits that only grow through a history of honest, distinct work, so a nebula of freshly spun fake accounts cannot instantly flood the market.
